title.value: Orchestrate parallel AI workers to build products from a spec

introduction.value:
A developer has a lead orchestrator agent assign modules to sub-orchestrators and workers from a large spec, building a consumer shop, a SaaS and Steam games.
·
Nov 15, 2026

method.value: Starting from a large spec, a lead orchestrator agent (Claude Fable) reviews it, tracks work in git, and hands well-scoped independent modules, each with its own repository, to sub-orchestrators. Those spawn workers, using cheaper ChatGPT and Google agents. A self-hosted CI/CD and git, plus a custom MCP for swarm communication, run on Hetzner servers using each provider's harness.

outcome.value: A Rust-engine Steam game is nearly ready to release, and the shop and SaaS are planned for year end. A two-hour DeepSeek test burned $40. The author is unsure whether it is truly worthwhile or just burning tokens.

notes.value: Subscriptions cost about $1k a month combined; test suites run slowly because the lead agent writes huge ones, so a fast self-hosted CI/CD build server matters.

source_text.body:
Orchestrate parallel AI workers to build products from a spec
A developer has a lead orchestrator agent assign modules to sub-orchestrators and workers from a large spec, building a consumer shop, a SaaS and Steam games.
·
Nov 15, 2026
Done with
CC
Claude Code
GP
ChatGPT
What they did
Starting from a large spec, a lead orchestrator agent (Claude Fable) reviews it, tracks work in git, and hands well-scoped independent modules, each with its own repository, to sub-orchestrators. Those spawn workers, using cheaper ChatGPT and Google agents. A self-hosted CI/CD and git, plus a custom MCP for swarm communication, run on Hetzner servers using each provider's harness.
How it went
A Rust-engine Steam game is nearly ready to release, and the shop and SaaS are planned for year end. A two-hour DeepSeek test burned $40. The author is unsure whether it is truly worthwhile or just burning tokens.
Worth knowing
Subscriptions cost about $1k a month combined; test suites run slowly because the lead agent writes huge ones, so a fast self-hosted CI/CD build server matters.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Here is my spec for [product, e.g. small web shop or indie game]: [paste spec or file path]. Break it into independent modules, write a short brief for each with inputs, outputs and acceptance tests, then work through them using sub-agents in parallel where they don't depend on each other. When all modules pass their tests and are integrated, give me a summary of what was built and what is left, and ask before deleting any files or deploying anything.
